previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, ICD placement, diabetes, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for acute dyspnea on exertion and leg weakness. Symptoms were likely due to mild volume overload from acute on chronic systolic heart failure, supported by elevated BNP, bilateral lung crackles, and radiographic evidence of mild pulmonary edema. He also had a productive cough suggestive of bronchitis. He received intravenous furosemide with resolution of symptoms and was able to ambulate without difficulty. Renal function was initially impaired with a creatinine of 1.7, improving to 1.6 during the stay. Lisinopril was held due to kidney concerns, with plans for outpatient reevaluation. Daytime somnolence was attributed to a high dose of imipramine, which was reduced at discharge. He was discharged home with instructions on weight monitoring, fluid and sodium restriction, and follow-up for lab work and psychiatric evaluation.

FINDINGS:  Frontal and lateral views of the chest were obtained.  The
left-sided AICD is seen with leads extending to the expected position of the
right ventricle.  Diffuse interstitial markings are again seen, most
prominently in the lung bases, slightly increased as compared to the prior
study, but somewhat similar compared to ___.  Relative lucency in the
upper lungs likely reflects pulmonary emphysema.  No pleural effusion or
pneumothorax is seen.  The cardiac and mediastinal silhouettes are stable with
unchanged moderate cardiomegaly and tortuous aorta.  Mild degenerative changes
are again seen along the visualized thoracolumbar spine.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Likely interstitial pulmonary edema, slightly increased since the prior
study.
